what: Every candidate route, scored. Lower is better.
formula: inputs*10 + human*3 + failure*2 + risk*6 - coverage*2 - recover*3 - drift*4

candidates.name: Push, and that is the instruction
candidates.why: Zero inputs, and every output comes from ONE commit - so the live demo and the released build cannot disagree.

candidates.name: Push, then press build yourself
candidates.why: Works, but the demo and the release can drift apart because they are two commits.

candidates.name: Describe it, then it runs itself
candidates.why: One input. Everything after it is already wired, and every workflow is a CALLER, so a fix reaches all of them.

candidates.name: Fully automatic, no input at all
candidates.why: Zero inputs sounds best until you ask who wrote the spec. Guessing the requirements is not automation, it is a coin toss with a release attached.

candidates.name: Do it all by hand
candidates.why: Every step is a decision, and the workflows are hand-copied - which is how a release got deleted once.

candidates.name: Diagnose, heal, audit, learn - on a schedule
candidates.why: Zero inputs. It is the only route that catches a workflow which runs on time and fails every time.

candidates.name: Watch the Actions page and fix what is red
candidates.why: This is what happened before: three workflows failed silently and nothing said so.

candidates.name: Press Run on the app's pipeline
candidates.why: One press, one commit, every output. The pipeline is the same one a push uses, so nothing is special-cased.

candidates.name: Tag it and let the tag drive
candidates.why: A tag is a second source of truth; the demo can end up on a different commit than the release.
